title: Some methods for classification and analysis of multivariate observations
summary: J. MacQueen published 'Some methods for classification and analysis of multivariate observations' in the Proceedings of the Fifth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability in 1967. The paper describes a process for partitioning an N-dimensional population into k sets and explicitly calls the process 'k-means.'
significance: A documented 1967 publication milestone for the k-means method, represented strictly as a publication event rather than an invention or priority claim.

verification.note: The University of California, Berkeley digital archive preserves MacQueen's original proceedings paper and its text explicitly states that the described partitioning process is called 'k-means.' Independent National Diet Library / CiNii bibliographic metadata records the publication year as 1967, in the Proceedings of the Fifth Berkeley Symposium, volume 1, pages 281-297, University of California Press. The Berkeley archive also exposes the symposium session dates spanning 1965-1966, which are not treated here as the publication date. This candidate therefore preserves year-only publication precision and does not assert an invention date, first-ever claim, development geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edge.
